turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, yeah, it's nice to meet you too. Um, so, I've been thinking about coming in for a little while now, actually. It's just... well, I'm 21, I'm finishing up my bachelor's, and I'm at this stage where I'm doing a lot of, you know, important paperwork and higher-level stuff. But what finally made me actually pick up the phone and come in today is that... well, I just keep turning in these applications, or like, my research notes for my professors, and they always have these really small but just incredibly embarrassing mistakes in them. 

Like, for example, the other day I submitted this thing and I had completely mislabeled an artwork date. Just wrote down the wrong era, basically, which is a huge deal in my field. Or I'll be filling out a really important application and I'll just skip an entire question without even realizing it. And the most frustrating part about the whole thing—and this is what really gets to me, honestly—is that I honestly thought I had checked them. Like, I will sit there, look over the whole page, read it top to bottom, tell myself it looks perfect, and then the second I hand it over, someone points out this glaring error. It makes me look so careless, and I really do care about the work, I just... I don't know how I keep missing this stuff when I'm staring right at it, you know? It's just been driving me crazy.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient reports repeatedly making small, careless mistakes on important paperwork and research notes, such as mislabeling dates or skipping questions, despite reviewing them.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been making these kinds of careless mistakes in different parts of your life since you were a child?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, actually, I have. It’s funny you ask about when I was a kid because my mom and I were just talking about this the other day, and she was reminding me about how it used to be back in elementary school. It was always the same story, honestly. Like, every parent-teacher conference, the teachers would sit down with my parents and say, "Oh, he’s got such great ideas, he’s so creative, he really understands the material," but then there was always this big "but." 

And the "but" was always about the little things. I would do the work, like I’d actually sit down and finish a worksheet, but then I’d just completely forget to turn it in. It would just sit in my desk or get crumpled up at the bottom of my backpack. Or I’d lose the instruction sheet for a project the second it was handed to me, and I’d end up doing the whole thing wrong because I missed some tiny, crucial detail about the formatting or the due date. 

It got to the point where my parents literally had to sit down with me every single night and physically unpack my backpack, piece by piece, just to make sure I wasn’t missing anything important. If they didn’t do that, things just disappeared into the void. And even with them checking, I’d still somehow manage to skip over questions on tests or forget to put my name on my paper. So, yeah, it’s definitely not a new thing, which is part of why it’s so frustrating now. I feel like I should have outgrown it by now, you know? Like, I'm 21, I shouldn't need someone checking my backpack anymore, but it feels like the same exact problem, just with higher stakes.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient describes missing tiny, crucial details, skipping questions on tests, and forgetting to put their name on papers.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient mentions keeping worksheets crumpled at the bottom of their backpack and needing their parents to unpack and organize it every night.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly states they would lose instruction sheets for projects the second they were handed out.

turns.doctor_question: When you read something, do you often skip words or lines without noticing?
turns.patient_response:
Um, skipping words or lines... you know, I actually don't think I do that. At least, not that I've ever really noticed. Like, when I'm reading, especially for my classes, because obviously there's a ton of reading in an art history program, I feel like I'm actually reading every single word. I'll sit there with my highlighter, and I'll go line by line, and I feel like I'm processing it all. 

I mean, sometimes I'll get to the bottom of the page and realize I have absolutely no idea what I just read, and I have to go back and read the whole page over again, which takes forever and is super annoying when you have like fifty pages to get through by Tuesday. But it's not like my eyes are physically skipping over the words or dropping down a line by mistake. It's more like the words go in, but my brain just... doesn't record them? But as far as actually skipping text, no, I don't think so. I'm pretty sure I read the words in order, I just don't always retain them, if that makes sense. But yeah, skipping lines isn't really something I've caught myself doing.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes reading a whole page and realizing they have no idea what they just read, which indicates a difficulty in sustaining attention during tasks.
